record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: For a random N-point input in Ω⊂R^d, does the Steiner-tree length have asymptotics βN^((d−1)/d), with β depending on Ω and on the random model?

evidence.quote: Question 2.9. Does the length of a Steiner tree for a random N-point input in Ω⊂R^d have asymptotics βN^(d−1)/d, where β is a constant depending on Ω and the random model?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded domain with $d \geq 2$. For a finite set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, let $\mathrm{St}(S)$ denote the length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure) of a Steiner tree of $S$, i.e. a connected set of minimal total length containing $S$ (one is allowed to add auxiliary "Steiner" points outside $S$). Fix a random model that produces an $N$-point random sample $X_N = \{X_1, \dots, X_N\} \subset \Omega$ (for instance, $N$ i.i.d. points drawn from a probability density on $\Omega$, or the points of a Poisson point process of intensity $N/|\Omega|$ on $\Omega$, or more general spatial models).

Question: Does there exist a constant $\beta = \beta(\Omega, \text{model}) > 0$ such that
$$\frac{\mathrm{St}(X_N)}{N^{(d-1)/d}} \longrightarrow \beta \qquad \text{as } N \to \infty,$$
where convergence holds almost surely (or in expectation)? Identify the class of admissible random models for which such asymptotics hold, and describe how $\beta$ depends on $\Omega$ and on the model.
artifact.category_tag: Random Steiner trees / subadditive Euclidean functionals
artifact.status_search_result: For i.i.d. uniform (and more generally absolutely continuous) samples in a bounded region of $\mathbb{R}^d$, the asymptotics $\mathrm{St}(X_N)/N^{(d-1)/d} \to \beta(d)\int_\Omega f(x)^{(d-1)/d}\,dx$ are classical, following from the Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley theorem (1959) and Steele's theory of subadditive Euclidean functionals, which explicitly covers the Steiner tree as one of the standard functionals. For more general (e.g. stationary ergodic, dependent, or non-absolutely-continuous) random models, the analogous BHH-type law is known to fail in some cases (counterexamples exist for ergodic sequences), and the precise class of random models for which the Steiner tree obeys such asymptotics remains an open question.

status_evidence.title: On Steiner's network problem (Mathematika)
status_evidence.snippet: BHH-type asymptotic bound applies to the Steiner tree problem as number of terminals increases.
status_evidence.claim: Classical BHH-type asymptotics established for Steiner trees on uniform random points.

status_evidence.title: Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley Theorem for Stationary Ergodic Sequences: a Counterexample
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexample showing BHH does not extend to all stationary ergodic sequences.
status_evidence.claim: General random models can fail the BHH-type asymptotics, so the question is open beyond the i.i.d./Poisson setting.

status_evidence.title: An asymptotic determination of the minimum spanning tree and minimum matching constants
status_evidence.snippet: MST, matching, and Steiner functionals scale almost surely as constant times n^((d-1)/d).
status_evidence.claim: Subadditive Euclidean functional theory yields the $N^{(d-1)/d}$ asymptotics for the Steiner functional in the i.i.d. case.
